original_test_intent: Run the approved stress-ng CPU workload for8 hours and verify continued responsiveness with no unexpected kernel, hardware or system-log errors.
original_method: Snapshot logs and health without clearing; validate stress-ng/version,225-worker relationship to topology, duration and limits; run tracked workload with live monitoring/hard timeout; preserve complete output/logs; stop processes, restore approved profile and obtain verdict.
manual_activity: Owner approves worker/duration/safety envelope and operator confirms cooling/power readiness; agent may run tracked stress afterward.
required_inputs: Verified stress-ng version/checksum and supported options
Approved worker count including whether literal225 is valid for topology and8-hour duration/timeout
CPU topology, current workloads, isolation and log/storage capacity
Governor/power restoration, cleanup, recovery and invalid-run policy
safety_requirements: Require explicit load/duration approval and cooling/power headroom
Track PID/session with hard timeout and live telemetry
Abort on limits, telemetry loss, OOM/ECC/watchdog/kernel error or unresponsiveness
No auto rerun/reboot or silent worker/profile/governor changes
agent_execution_scope: Validate package/profile and collect baseline evidence
Run exact approved tracked stress with complete untrimmed logs and telemetry
Terminate stress/monitors, restore approved state and verify health
Do not clear logs, substitute short cpu0 profile, tail output, rerun or issue verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Not equivalent: cpu0/300s differs from225/8h, tail removes evidence and unsafe SSH is prohibited.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After approval, run tracked stress-ng with approved worker count and8h or explicitly changed duration, metrics, hard timeout and complete logs; preserve rather than clear kernel logs.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: 225 workers,8h, stress-ng,30/500 fields and workable/error-free criterion are preserved as approval inputs.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use topology-bounded workers, tracked lifecycle, non-destructive log snapshots and live abort controller.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Removes evidence destruction, adds profile validation, telemetry, thresholds and cleanup.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A5-minute all-CPU run cannot establish the source's8-hour/225-worker endurance.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Oversubscription can distort load and responsiveness; long CPU saturation can throttle or impact services.

project_override_considerations: Any worker/duration change must be explicitly approved and reported as changed coverage; no automatic normalization to CPU count.
expected_evidence: Host/CPU topology, OS/kernel and stress-ng version/checksum
Exact approved worker/duration/timeout command and tracked status
Cleanup/restoration, final health and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Stress-ng workload and acceptance are understandable. `dmesg -c` is an unsafe source action, and worker/duration limits are readiness inputs, but the test intent is not contradictory.

blocked_analysis.analysis: stress-ng, profile and safety controls can be supplied; execution is feasible after confirmation.

review_improvement: Preserves the long-stress intent while preventing kernel-log destruction and silent short-profile substitution.
independent_technical_reasoning: `dmesg -c` consumes the kernel ring buffer and destroys the baseline needed to attribute errors. Also,225 workers may either match or oversubscribe the CPU topology, whereas cpu0 selects online CPUs; neither is interchangeable without approval. Duration and worker count are coverage parameters, and complete health telemetry is needed to distinguish throttling from stability.
